- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift but fail to capture sharp spikes or sudden drops in true values.
- Overshoots occur after large upward spikes in history (e.g., 80+ values), where model continues rising while true value corrects downward.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds upward trend longer than observed.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the first 10–15 days, then catch up or overcorrect.
- Model exhibits “flat plateau” behavior in early forecast days, missing volatility or sudden reversals.
- High volatility in true values (e.g., 80–90 range) is not reflected in model’s smooth, linear progression.
- Model tends to over-predict in the final 5–10 days of forecast, especially when true values show downward correction.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the short-term (1–3 days ahead) and too conservative in the medium-term (5–10 days ahead).
